_help: Day 3, room 7: the front garden, 'Where it began' (1938-1948), and the end of the story. The hopscotch pattern and the house number for the letterbox; Chloé on her leash; she digs up the time capsule; the year on Maman's rose sign plus ten for the gate. The last letter opens when the gate does. See docs/STORY.md.

locks._why: Maman planted the roses the year Céline was born (the sign says 1938); she buried the tin at ten, and 'the gate has kept that year': 1948.
hints: How old was she when she buried the tin? And when was she born?
Maman's rose sign and the time capsule belong to the garden gate.

locks._why: The chalk squares grow by one more each time (+1, +2, +3...): 16, then 22.
hints: Little Céline's hopscotch has a rule.
Look at how much each number grows.

locks._why: Maman's number: the house (12, on the letterbox), then the last square Céline ever reached at hopscotch (22).
hints: Where did Maman keep the old dog's leash? Behind a number only they knew.
The house number and the last hopscotch square belong to the letterbox.

locks._why: Chloé scratches at the gate for her leash (in the letterbox). Happy, she drops a memory.
hints: Chloé keeps scratching at the gate.
She wants her leash, and it was in the letterbox.
Select the leash, then tap Chloé.

locks._why: The time capsule is buried under Maman's roses; Chloé digs it up.
hints: Something old is buried by the gate.
Chloé could dig under the roses.
Tap Chloé, then tap the soil under the roses.

clues.text: The house number, painted on the letterbox by Céline's father: 12.
Half hidden among the roses, a little enamel sign, chipped at the corners: FOR CÉLINE · 1938.
